value: Nothing that requires a river ford above the knee

context.value: We have done hut-to-hut in the Chic-Chocs once before, in fair weather. Neither of us has navigated in cloud and we would rather not learn on this trip.

candidates.title: Refuge Le Carouge
candidates.summary: A bunkroom hut on the traverse, wood stove, no plumbing. Reserved through SEPAQ and it goes early for the late-August weekends.

place.name: Refuge Le Carouge
place.locality: Parc national de la Gaspésie, Québec

candidates.title: Mont Albert traverse, southern approach
candidates.summary: Up the south face to the plateau and across it. About 14 km with the climb front-loaded, which suits a party carrying three nights of food.

place.name: Mont Albert
place.locality: Parc national de la Gaspésie, Québec

candidates.title: Plateau weather and the caribou closure
candidates.summary: The plateau makes its own weather and can be in cloud with the valley clear, which is the navigation case this party said it wanted to avoid. Parts of the range close seasonally for the caribou herd — the park authority is the only source that can say which, and it must be checked before departure.

place.name: Mont Albert plateau
place.locality: Parc national de la Gaspésie, Québec

candidates.title: Park entry and hut reservation through SEPAQ
candidates.summary: Backcountry huts are reservation-only and entry is per person per day. Both are bought in the same transaction, which is the one deadline this trip actually has.
